qa_pairs.question: For Fall 2026, when does the standard add/drop period end and what is the census date?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The standard add/drop period for Fall 2026 ends at 17:00 on August 28, and the census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum attendance requirement, and may a course syllabus change that threshold?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A syllabus may set a higher threshold when accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice requires it, but it may not set a lower threshold.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: What credit and GPA requirements make an undergraduate academically eligible to graduate?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An undergraduate must complete at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

qa_pairs.question: Is multi-factor authentication required for the student portal, and will staff ever ask for my password or one-time code?

qa_pairs.question: My tuition balance is still unpaid after the grace period. What fee applies and can I still register for the next term?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance. After it, an unpaid balance receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. A student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold, so the hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance until it is cleared. It does not remove the student from courses that were already confirmed.

contexts.text: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed.
A student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold.

qa_pairs.question: The standard add/drop period is over. What approvals and payment does a late add need, and what happens if I pay the fee late?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The late-add window runs from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add. The fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: Which terms trigger a Merit Scholarship renewal review, and what must the recipient achieve to renew?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Renewal is assessed after each Fall and Spring term; Summer enrolment does not trigger a separate renewal review. To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

contexts.text: Renewal is assessed after each Fall and Spring term; Summer enrolment does not trigger a separate renewal review.

qa_pairs.question: If I leave a Fall 2026 course after the census date, what appears on my record and what is the last day to do it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Before or on census the portal records a drop, but after census the course receives a W grade. For Fall 2026 the last day to withdraw with a W is October 30. After that deadline a withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition, and stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.

contexts.text: Before or on census, the portal records a drop. After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`. After that deadline, withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition. Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: How much Fall 2026 tuition is reversed if I drop one course on August 25, and how much if I drop it on September 2?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A drop on August 25 falls within the standard add/drop period, which ends on August 28, so 100% of that course tuition is reversed. September 2 is after add/drop but on or before the September 4 census date, so 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: I think my final grade was calculated wrongly. What step comes first, and what deadline and grounds apply to a formal grade appeal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor, and the student must request clarification within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.
A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor.

qa_pairs.question: A Merit Scholarship holder takes an approved medical leave, and later a voluntary leave for a job. What happens to the award in each case?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. Either way a standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms and the request must be submitted before the census date with programme approval.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. qa_pairs.question: A student completed 75% of assessed work and was passing before a documented emergency. Can an incomplete be granted, and what happens if the remaining work is never submitted?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An I incomplete may be granted because at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term, and if no grade is submitted by that deadline the I converts to F unless an approved extension exists.

qa_pairs.question: A scholarship student is approved for a medical withdrawal. What money is returned, and how late may a retroactive medical leave still be filed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund, and scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated. A retroactive medical leave request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the last documented participation; a later request requires evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period.

contexts.text: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation. Later requests require evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period.

qa_pairs.question: A student has finished all coursework but still has an unpaid balance and a pending grade appeal on a required course. Can the degree be conferred, and does walking at commencement prove graduation?

A pending grade appeal may also delay conferral because the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold. Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred.
